title: Rectangular section
spec: Create a new coordinate system with Euler angles set to zero and a translation vector also set to zero. Next, draw a two-dimensional sketch on a new face. The sketch should consist of a closed loop made up of four lines. The first line starts at the origin and ends at coordinates [0.0326, 0.0]. The second line extends from this point to [0.0326, 0.0326]. The third line then moves to [0.0, 0.0326], and the fourth line completes the loop back to the origin. After drawing the sketch, apply a scaling factor of 0.0326 to the entire sketch. Rotate the sketch plane using the same Euler angles and translate it using the same vector as initially set. Finally, extrude the scaled and transformed sketch along the normal direction by 0.75 units to create a solid body. The dimensions of this rectangular section are 0.032608695652173905 units in length and width, and 0.75 units in height.

reference.label: Reference (dataset)
reference.code:
import cadquery as cq

# Create a new workplane
r = cq.Workplane("XY")

# Create a sketch on the XY plane
r = r.box(0.0326, 0.0326, 0.75, centered=(False, False, False))

# The final model is represented as 'r'

lanes.label: GLM-5.3 Flash (high)
lanes.code:
import cadquery as cq

# Define the dimensions from the bounding box
x_dim = 0.0326
y_dim = 0.0326
z_dim = 0.7500

# The part is a simple square-column (prismatic bar) extruded along Z.
# Both the TOP and ISOMETRIC views show a plain square cross-section,
# and the FRONT/RIGHT views show a plain rectangular profile with no
# holes, slots, steps or other features.

r = (
    cq.Workplane("XY")
    .rect(x_dim, y_dim)
    .extrude(z_dim)
)

import cadquery as cq

# Create a new workplane
r = cq.Workplane("XY")

# Define the sketch for the top face
r = r.rect(0.0326, 0.0326) \
     .edges("(>X and |Y) or (<X and |Y)") \
     .fillet(0.0013)

# Extrude the sketch to create the body
r = r.extrude(0.75)

# The final model is represented as 'r'
